title: Darrell Royal: The Sooner Who Became a Texas Coaching Legend
question: Did Texas coach Darrell Royal play football at Oklahoma?
answer: Darrell Royal, an OU quarterback and defensive back from 1946 to 1949, coached Texas from 1957 to 1976 and won national titles in 1963, 1969 and 1970.
summary: Darrell Royal starred at OU from 1946 to 1949, then coached Texas from 1957 to 1976, won three national titles and entered the College Football Hall of Fame.
body: It is one of the great ironies of the Red River rivalry: the coach who built Texas into a national power learned the game in crimson. Darrell Royal, born in Hollis, Oklahoma, played at OU from 1946 through 1949, the last three seasons under Bud Wilkinson, lining up at quarterback, defensive back and punter.

He was an All-American in 1949 and set Sooner records for career interceptions (18) and interceptions in a single game (three, against Oklahoma A&M in 1947), along with a school-record 96-yard punt return. The Sooners went 36-6-1 during his four seasons and won back-to-back Sugar Bowls, edging North Carolina 14-6 and then blanking LSU 35-0 in January 1950.

After assistant jobs and stops at Edmonton in the CFL, Mississippi State and Washington, Royal took over at Texas in 1957. Over 20 seasons he went 167-47-5, won 11 Southwest Conference titles, led the Longhorns to 16 bowl games and claimed national championships in 1963, 1969 and 1970. Texas introduced the wishbone under Royal in 1968, the same offense that later powered Oklahoma's great teams.
Royal also served as Texas athletic director, retiring in 1980, and entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 1983. In 1996 Texas renamed its stadium Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium.
Royal died in November 2012. Sooner fans may never cheer his Texas teams, but they can claim, with some pride, that one of college football's greatest coaches got his start in Norman.
